Subject: Request: temporary SLO waiver + monthly credit allocation

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal/procurement team is pushing for stricter uptime (99.99%) given we run payment reconciliation jobs at peak times, but our infra folks also asked whether Redwood can add a temporary carveout while we migrate to a dedicated pool. Specifically we need:

- A temporary SLO exception for the first 90 days of production (we call this the migration period).
- Clear monthly credit math if uptime dips below 99.95 during that period.
- A cap on total credits per month and a maintenance carveout window.

I've attached our Q3 usage so you can see burst patterns. Can you propose language we can include in the MSA and a sample calculation for credits?

Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO waiver + monthly credit allocation

Tim —

Appreciate the context and the data — helpful. High level proposal below; I copied Laura (contracts) and Marissa (CS) so we can align on operational details.

Proposal (initial, subject to legal redline):
1) Migration period: 90 days from production cutover where Arborlyst may request a Temporary SLO Waiver.
2) Baseline SLO during waiver: 99.90% availability. After the 90-day period Redwood will revert to the contracted baseline (we can discuss 99.95/99.99 if you want a stepped ramp).
3) Monthly service credits during waiver: tiered prorata formula based on minutes of unavailability beyond the 99.90% threshold: 
   - Unavailability > 0 and <= 60 minutes in month: credit = 3% of monthly Redwood invoice
   - >60 and <= 240 minutes: credit = 8% of monthly Redwood invoice
   - >240 minutes: credit = 20% of monthly Redwood invoice
   - Credit cap during waiver: 40% of monthly invoice
4) Maintenance carveout: regular maintenance windows (pre-scheduled with >=72h notice) are excluded from availability calculations. Emergency maintenance will be communicated via status.redwood.com and will be considered for carveout on a case-by-case basis.
5) Fallbacks: during capacity constraints we will offer automatic routing to a compatible model variant (may impact latency).

Next steps: Laura, can you draft redline language matching the above? Marissa — we'll need an ops runbook for scheduling a dedicated pool and a handoff checklist so Arborlyst can hit the 90-day target.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Tim —

Thanks. Attached is a first-pass redline that mirrors Connor's proposal but with contract-ready phrasing. A couple of clarifications we need from you to finalize the drafting:

1) Do you want the 90-day clock to start on the first production request (cutover) or on the date the dedicated pool is provisioned?
2) For the credit calculation above we use the customer invoice as the denominator. If you prefer a token-usage-derived credit (e.g., credit tied to billing for inference units impacted), say so and we can provide a sample.
3) Please confirm your preferred maintenance window (we typically propose a weekly 2-hour window between 02:00–06:00 local time). If Arborlyst requires a locked maintenance blackout for specific hours, we'll need to account for that in capacity planning and pricing.

If those look good I can push a redline against your MSA and share a DocuSign link.

Laura Bennett

Laura / Connor —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Arborlyst confirms: 

- Start of 90-day migration period = production cutover (we will notify you when traffic begins routing).
- We prefer the monthly invoice-based credit (simpler for our finance team).
- Maintenance window: we can accept your proposed weekly 02:00–04:00 UTC window for the migration period.

The credit tiers look reasonable. Two small asks before we sign:
1) Can Redwood add a one-time onboarding credit if we experience >120 minutes of unplanned unavailability during the first 30 days? Suggested amount: an automatic 5% credit for that first month only.
2) We need DocuSign-ready language for the waiver clause so procurement can get approvals — ideally today or tomorrow.

If you can accept the onboarding credit we can push this through procurement and route the MSA for signature.

—Tim
